newsitem.title: UK: British priest advocates theft from supermarkets.
newsitem.headline: British priest advocates theft from supermarkets.

text.p: A Church of England priest sparked a row on Saturday by saying he approved of shoplifting from supermarkets.
The Reverend John Papworth told parishioners at a meeting to discuss crime that large supermarkets were destroying community life and that it was therefore justified to steal from them.
"I don't regard it as stealing. I regard it as a badly needed reallocation of economic resources," Papworth said.
Britain's supermarket chains had put small grocers out of business, created unemployment and encouraged greed and consumerism with their advertising campaigns, he argued.
His remarks were immediately denounced by the Church of England.
"He clearly does not speak for the Church of England and indeed his comments have already been disowned by his bishop and his vicar," a Church of England spokesman told BBC radio.
Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard joined the condemnation, calling Papworth's comments "disgraceful."
But Papworth, a 75-year-old part-time priest in the wealthy north London district of St John's Wood, was unrepentant.

"When you talk about stealing you can only steal from a person, you can only have a moral relationship with a person, you don't have a moral relationship with things -- that is a power relationship," he told the BBC.
"Jesus said love your neighbour; he didn't say love Marks and Spencers," said Papworth, referring to one of Britain's biggest chain store groups.

It is not the first time the priest has run into controversy. He was imprisoned, along with philosopher Bertrand Russell, in the 1960s for his part in a campaign against nuclear weapons and was also jailed in the U.S. for taking part in a march for black rights.
